response.justification: Broad, 15+ year engineering career with genuine high-throughput distributed systems exposure (Sociomantic/dunnhumby: micro-services handling millions of HTTP requests per second, low-latency async work) and current hands-on involvement in AI-agent infrastructure, MCP code generators, and agentic tooling — which maps directly to the AI-native mindset the role treats as baseline. TypeScript depth is excellent and the software-craftsmanship background (TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based development, teaching/workshops) suggests the technical influence expected at staff level. The main gap is the must-have 'strong Python': it appears nowhere in the skills list or any role, while the resume's polyglot strength is concentrated in TypeScript/Node and DLang — effectively inverting the language priority of the job. Distributed-systems depth is also several years in the past, with recent roles skewing toward product/full-stack work, and there is little concrete evidence of scaled technical strategy, cross-functional stakeholder management, or on-call/incident ownership. Worth a screen to probe Python fluency and recent architectural scope, but not a clear-cut fit on paper.
strengths: Real high-throughput, low-latency distributed systems experience at ad-tech scale
Current hands-on work on AI-agent infrastructure, MCP tooling, and agentic workflows
Deep TypeScript/Node expertise plus strong testing and design-pattern craftsmanship
concerns: No Python evidence anywhere, despite it being a must-have skill
Distributed-systems depth is dated (2018–2020); recent roles are product/full-stack
Little demonstrated technical strategy, stakeholder management, or on-call ownership
